title: What is known about 1RB0RD_1LC0LE_0RA0LB_1RC1RF_1LB1RD_0RC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RD_1LC0LE_0RA0LB_1RC1RF_1LB1RD_0RC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine's tape is a row of blocks of 001: all but the last are frozen, the last is rebuilt again and again by a bouncer that lives inside it. Phase P1 of that bouncer (any number of bounces, all sizes) is proved in Lean; the rule for a whole return of the head, a' = a + b + 7, is measured, not proved. Halting needs the head in D on two 1s side by side; that never happens in the first 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 25,666 cells have been visited and 8,997 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.131). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.387).

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: Lean proves, for every count and every tape around, how the head crosses a block of 001 leftward in C (9 steps per copy, rewriting it as 100), and one whole bounce of the inner bouncer of the live block: from L 1 1 (001)^m 0 (001)^(j+4) 0 (110)^(k+1) 1 1 0 A> 0^∞ the machine reaches the same shape with m+3, j−3 and k+1 in 36j + 24k + 151 steps (bounce_tail).

claims.title: Phase P1 of the live block, for every number of bounces
claims.text: Write Live(x, y, z) for the tape L 1 1 (001)^x 0 (001)^y (011)^z 0 A> 0^∞ (any L). Lean proves (x, y+1+3n, z+2) → (x+3n, y+1, z+2+n) for every x, y, z, n (p1, an induction over bounce_tail), and from an empty right part (x, y+6+3n, 0) → (x+4+3n, y+2, n+2) (p1_from0, using the first two bounces bounce_z0 (12y + 35 steps) and bounce_z1 (36y + 127 steps)). So phase P1 always ends with the middle part y equal to 2, 3 or 4.

claims.title: The tape is a row of frozen blocks and one live block
claims.text: At every return of the head to the left end (state C there, 135 times in 109 steps) the tape is C>0 1 0 1 (100)^59 0^3 1 (100)^107 0 1^3 (001)^1452 0 (1001)^2 (001)^392 …: blocks of 001 separated by short walls. Every block but the last stays the same from then on (59, 107, 1452, 392, 165, 337, 837 in the run to 109); only the last one changes.

claims.title: Growth of the live block: a' = a + b + 7
claims.text: When the live block reads (001)^a (011)^b 01 at a left return, at the next left return it reads (001)^(a+b+7) (011)^(b'): (229,6) → (242,82) → (331,87) → (425,116) → (548,148) → (703,189) → (899,240) → (1146,306). b'/a' tends to about 0.27, so the block grows by a factor of about 1.27 per return, until it splits a new frozen block off.

claims.title: The inner bouncer's phase change
claims.text: Inside the live block, phase P1 moves 001s from the middle part to the left part until the middle part is used up: (100)^a (010)^b (110)^c becomes (100)^(a+3) (010)^(b−3) (110)^(c+1) each bounce (now proved for any number of bounces, see above). The following phase P2 then turns (a, 0, c) into (a', b', 0) with a' + b' = a + c + 1 and a' = c − d for a constant d that depends on the block to its left (d = 39 for four phases in a row from step 4·106 on). In the coordinates of Live: from (x, 2, z) the next empty-right configuration is (x', y', 0) with x' + y' = x + z + 3 in all 9 cases seen in 109 steps; x' = z + 1 while there is no frozen block to the left (4 cases up to step 2·104), x' = z + 1 − 41 for 3 phases (steps 4·106 to 2·107) and z + 1 − 333 for 2 (steps 5·108 to 6·108). P2 reaches the left end of the tape, so it is not a rule about the live block alone; it is not proved.

claims.title: Never one step from a halt
claims.text: The machine halts when F reads a 1, and F is entered only from D reading a 1 (D1 → 1RF). In the first 3·10<sup>6</sup> steps D reads a 1 3,851 times, always with a 0 to its right, so F always reads 0.

claims.title: Size of the tape description (family screen)
claims.text: At the 8 records between 2.7·10<sup>8</sup> and 2.0·10<sup>10</sup> steps (first new leftmost or rightmost cell after each threshold 10<sup>6</sup>·4^k) the tape has 9,496 to 118,465 visited cells and compresses to 29 to 37 level-2 tokens (repeats of a word of at most 40 cells, then repeats of groups of such tokens).

claims.title: Proposed family: F01, periodic blocks driven by a bounded engine
claims.text: The description grows slowly if at all: 29 to 37 level-2 tokens at every record from 2.7·108 to 2·1010 steps, and 10 to 32 runs in the macro simulator (blocks of 3 cells) at the sampled records from 106 to 9·1012 steps. At step 19,693,788,191 the tape has frozen blocks of 60, 107, 1,452, 394, 165, 338, 838 and 12,270 copies of 100 or 001 and a live part (001)^21588 (011)^2262. Within a level this is the F01 shape (a live block with a short engine, phase P1 already proved in Lean), and a level ends with the block frozen, as in 1RB0LC_0RC0RF_1RD0LE_1LA1RA_1LC1RB_0RB---. The list of frozen blocks is not bounded: 5 blocks at 7.6·107 steps, 8 at 2·1010.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Deciding it would need the rule for a whole return of the head (phase P2 and the splitting of the live block, which both involve the frozen blocks to the left) as a map on the block sizes, proved, and then an argument that its outcome never puts D next to two 1s. Phase P1 is now proved; the splitting looks like a Collatz-like condition on the sizes modulo 3.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine builds a row of blocks of 001, freezes them one after another, and keeps working on the last one with a smaller bouncer that lives inside it. This page shows the pieces, the rule that the measurements follow, and what is proved.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 25,666 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: A row of frozen blocks and one live block
html: Look at the tape each time the head comes back to the left end. It is a row of blocks of 001, each followed by a short wall:

((001)^5 is 001 written five times; C> is the head, in state C.) The blocks 59, 107, 1452, 392, 165, 337, 837 never change again once a newer block exists: they are frozen. Only the last block, here (001)^3680 … (011)^1055, is live.

sections.heading: A bouncer inside the last block
html: Between two visits to the left end the head never leaves the live block. Inside it a second bouncer runs. Seen each time the head is at the right end in state A, the block is three parts, (100)^a (010)^b (110)^c, and one bounce does

e.g. at step 4,422,876 the end of the tape is (001)^61 0^3 (100)^263 (101)^5 10 A>0 and six bounces later (001)^79 0^3 (100)^245 (101)^11 10 A>0. This bounce is proved in Lean for all sizes (bounce_tail in lean/Rules.lean), and so is the whole phase: any number of bounces, starting from an empty right part (p1, p1_from0 in lean/P1.lean). It ends when the middle part is down to 2, 3 or 4 copies.

When the middle part runs out, a slower phase rebuilds it from the other two (measured: a' + b' = a + c + 1; how the total is shared between a' and b' depends on the frozen block to the left, because this phase runs to the left end of the tape; not proved). At the level of whole returns, the live block (001)^a (011)^b becomes (001)^(a+b+7)…, so it grows by about 27% per return: 331, 425, 548, 703, 899, 1146, … until a wall appears inside it and the left part freezes.

sections.heading: What a halt would need
html: The machine stops only when it is in F reading a 1, and it enters F only from D reading a 1. So a halt needs D>1 1: the head in D on a 1 that has another 1 to its right. In the first 3·106 steps D reads a 1 3,851 times and the next cell is always 0. In the block picture, a halt would need a wall of a shape that the splitting of the live block has never produced. Whether it ever does depends on the block sizes, probably modulo 3, through rules that are measured but not proved: the question is open.

sections.heading: Which family it belongs to
html: The 22 machines of family F09 (“bouncers over lists of counters, not yet classified”) were screened in one way. The machine runs from blank tape for 2·1010 steps; each time the tape reaches a new cell after a threshold, the tape is compressed twice: first repeats of one word, then repeats of groups of words. If the tape is a few growing blocks and a bounded rest, the number of level-2 tokens stays bounded while the tape grows. Everything in this section is observed in one run. None of it is proved.
Proposed family: F01, periodic blocks driven by a bounded engine (frozen blocks of 001 and one live block rebuilt by an inner bouncer).

The description grows slowly if at all: 29 to 37 level-2 tokens at every record from 2.7·108 to 2·1010 steps, and 10 to 32 runs in the macro simulator (blocks of 3 cells) at the sampled records from 106 to 9·1012 steps. At step 19,693,788,191 the tape has frozen blocks of 60, 107, 1,452, 394, 165, 338, 838 and 12,270 copies of 100 or 001 and a live part (001)^21588 (011)^2262.

Within a level this is the F01 shape (a live block with a short engine, phase P1 already proved in Lean), and a level ends with the block frozen, as in 1RB0LC_0RC0RF_1RD0LE_1LA1RA_1LC1RB_0RB---. The list of frozen blocks is not bounded: 5 blocks at 7.6·107 steps, 8 at 2·1010.
Next step. Prove the whole return a' = a + b + 7 (measured), then the F01 closure on (a, b) with the frozen list treated as arbitrary.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.131). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.387).
After 109 steps the tape spans 25,666 cells (64 left of the start, 14,996 right), with a density of 1s of 0.351.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: frozen blocks with a self-feeding growing tail
summary: A row of frozen blocks of 001 on the left and one live block on the right that a sub-bouncer keeps refilling: at each full return the live block (001)^a (011)^b becomes (001)^(a+b+7) (011)^b', and now and then it splits off a new frozen block.
